      <title>Libyan unity talks upended as warlord’s son linked to drone attacks on fuel facilities</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/03/libyan-unity-talks-warlord-son-linked-drone-attack-khalifa-haftar</link>
      <description><p>Western Libya’s GNU say working with Saddam Haftar ‘impossible’ as US-backed merger plan breaks down</p><p>Allegations that the son of the Libyan warlord Khalifa Haftar oversaw a “terror cell” that launched drone attacks on fuel storage facilities and power stations in western Libya have upended plans for the Tripoli-based government of national unity (GNU) to continue cooperating with Haftar on a plan to unify the country.</p><p>Saddam Haftar, the deputy commander of the so-called Libyan National Army (LNA), has increasingly been seen by the US as an important figure in its plans to unify Libyan security, judicial and political institutions.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/03/libyan-unity-talks-warlord-son-linked-drone-attack-khalifa-haftar">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Trump administration diverts human rights funds to push far-right agenda abroad</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/30/trump-state-department-human-rights-fund</link>
      <description><p>Support such as for white Afrikaners and anti-communism reveals how US is redefining what qualifies as human rights</p><p>With hours left before the funding expires, the Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175m of the state department’s flagship human rights fund to a slate of awards that includes a huge $40m grant for an anti-communism fund, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner rights in South Africa, a campaign against Brazil’s supreme court and programs that would reward ideological allies in Europe who protect “western civilizational norms”.</p><p>On Wednesday, the state department obligated the funds to the grantees hours before the deadline despite congressional concerns and requests not to do so, according to a source familiar with the negotiations. The state department declined to comment on questions from the Guardian specifically on whether it had obligated the funds and had “blown” holds from Congress due to concerns about the money’s use.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/30/trump-state-department-human-rights-fund">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>President announces measures amid anger at authorities over recent murders of women</p><p>South Africa’s president has called on men to take more responsibility for violence against women as he announced measures to tackle the problem, amid anger at authorities over a recent wave of murders.</p><p>Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged that not enough had been done to protect women.       <description><p>Sunday’s poll pits the leftist incumbent Lula against the son of a former far-right president convicted of staging a coup</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/02/brazil-election-lady-of-aparecida-lula-bolsonaro-row">‘No one disrespects Our Lady’: fears for Brazil’s patron saint grip country ahead of election</a></p></li></ul><p>Shortly after his <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/22/donald-trump-unga-speech">controversial speech</a> to the United Nations general assembly in September, Donald Trump gathered a dozen like-minded Latin American leaders and boasted that rightwing candidates had won all seven presidential elections held in the region since he began his second term.</p><p>“Everybody I’ve endorsed has won,” the US president said in New York to most of the leaders of the Shield of the Americas, an <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/07/an-ideological-guest-list-trump-invites-latin-americas-rightwing-leaders-to-florida-summit">anti-drug cartel coalition</a> of 15 countries governed by the right or far right.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/03/brazil-election-lula-bolsonaro-trump">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s former husband says he was ‘shocked’ by death of her ex-partner</title>

      <description><p>Ryan Anderson says he reached out to Blanchard’s father to offer support after apparent overdose death of Ken Urker</p><p>The ex-husband of Gypsy Rose Blanchard has said he was “shocked” by the recent <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/02/gypsy-rose-blanchard-ken-urker-dead">death</a> in Louisiana of her former partner Ken Urker – and that he would be there for Blanchard and her daughter “if she needs me”.</p><p>Ryan Anderson made those remarks during an appearance on <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LC3wxxYcmL8">The Sarah Fraser Show</a> podcast on Friday, providing a noteworthy reaction to the latest chapter involving Blanchard, who achieved an unusual level of celebrity in the US after spending time imprisoned for a role in the murder of her abusive mother in Missouri.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2026/oct/03/gypsy-rose-blanchard-former-husband">Continue reading...</a></description>
